Follow the Trend / Trade With the Trend.display_name: Follow the Trend / Trade With the Trend
Follow the Trend / Trade With the Trend.description: Take positions in the direction of the prevailing trend rather than fighting it. "The trend is your friend" is the single most repeated rule in the corpus.

Always Use a Stop-Loss.description: Set a price where you exit a losing trade before you enter it. It caps the damage from any single mistake.

Control Emotions: Avoid Fear and Greed.display_name: Control Emotions: Avoid Fear and Greed
Control Emotions: Avoid Fear and Greed.description: Fear makes traders exit winners early and greed makes them hold or oversize. Mechanical rules and self-awareness keep both in check.

Follow Your Trading Plan/System Without.display_name: Follow Your Trading Plan Without Deviation
Follow Your Trading Plan/System Without.description: Plan the trade, then trade the plan. Deviating mid-trade turns a tested system into guesswork.

Support and Resistance Levels.description: Prices tend to stall at levels where buyers or sellers stepped in before. Those levels frame entries, stops and targets.

Momentum Indicators (RSI, MACD, Stochast.description: Oscillators gauge the speed of price moves and flag overbought or oversold conditions.

Cut Losses Short, Let Winners Run.display_name: Cut Losses Short, Let Winners Run
Cut Losses Short, Let Winners Run.description: Small losses and large gains make a system profitable even with a win rate under 50%.

Use Moving Averages to Identify Trend.display_name: Use Moving Averages to Identify Trend
Use Moving Averages to Identify Trend.description: Price above a rising average signals an uptrend; crossovers of fast and slow averages mark changes.

Position Sizing Based on Risk.description: Size each position by the distance to your stop and the capital at risk, not by conviction.

Breakout Trading Above Resistance/Below.description: Enter when price clears resistance or breaks support on strength, and filter out false breakouts.

Have a Predefined Exit Plan Before Enter.description: Know your profit target and your stop before entry, so exits aren't decided under pressure.

Continuous Education and Self-Improvemen.description: Markets change; successful traders keep studying, reviewing mistakes and refining skills.

Avoid Overleveraging / Excessive Margin.description: Leverage magnifies losses as much as gains and is the most common cause of blown accounts.

Chart Patterns (Head and Shoulders, Tria.description: Head-and-shoulders, triangles, flags and channels signal likely continuation or reversal.

Discipline Beats Intelligence in Trading.description: Consistent execution of simple rules outperforms clever analysis applied erratically.

Risk-Reward Ratio Before Entering a Trad.description: Only take trades where the potential gain is a multiple of the risk, and know the system's expectancy.

Backtest a Trading System Before Using R.description: Test a system on historical data, including its maximum drawdown, before committing capital.

Diversify Across Uncorrelated Assets.description: Holding assets that don't move together reduces portfolio volatility without equally reducing return.

Patience: Wait for High-Probability Setu.description: Most of trading is waiting. When in doubt, stay out.

Fibonacci Retracement Levels.description: Pullbacks often stall near 38.2%, 50% or 61.8% of the prior move, which gives candidate entries and targets.

Liquidity Matters When Entering/Exiting.display_name: Liquidity Matters When Entering and Exiting
Liquidity Matters When Entering/Exiting.description: Thinly traded markets mean wide spreads and slippage; trade where you can get in and out cleanly.

Markets Are Cyclical (Bull and Bear Cycl.description: Bull and bear phases recur with the business cycle and crowd psychology.

Understand Implied Volatility Before Tra.display_name: Understand Implied Volatility Before Trading Options
Understand Implied Volatility Before Tra.description: An option's price depends heavily on expected volatility; buying when it is high can lose money even if direction is right.

Volume Confirms Price Action.description: Moves on rising volume are more trustworthy; accumulation and distribution show up in volume first.

Keep a Trading Journal.description: Recording every trade and your reasoning exposes recurring mistakes and real edge.

Manage Expectations: Trading Is Not Gamb.display_name: Manage Expectations: Trading Is Not Gambling
Manage Expectations: Trading Is Not Gamb.description: Aim for consistent modest returns and treat get-rich-quick claims as warning signs.

Never Risk More Than 1-2% of Capital Per.display_name: Never Risk More Than 1–2% Per Trade
Never Risk More Than 1-2% of Capital Per.description: A fixed small risk per trade lets you survive long losing streaks.

Long-Term Investing Beats Market Timing.description: Staying invested usually beats trying to call tops and bottoms, which few do reliably.

Currency Pairs Move on Interest Rate Dif.display_name: Currencies Move on Rate Differentials and News
Currency Pairs Move on Interest Rate Dif.description: Forex prices respond to interest-rate gaps, carry, central-bank action and data surprises.

Keep Trading Systems Simple.description: Few rules and few indicators hold up better out of sample; there is no holy-grail indicator.

Candlestick Patterns Signal Reversals/Co.description: Dojis, hammers, engulfing and star patterns signal short-term reversals or continuation.

Interest Rates Affect Asset Prices.description: Rising rates pressure bond and stock valuations; falling rates support them.

Hedge Positions With Options/Futures.description: Protective puts, collars and offsetting futures limit downside on existing holdings.

Use Multiple Timeframes for Confirmation.description: Check the higher timeframe's trend before acting on a signal from a shorter one.

Preserve Capital First, Profit Second.description: Only risk money you can afford to lose; staying in the game matters more than any single gain.

Don't Let Ego Affect Trading Decisions.description: Take responsibility, admit when you're wrong and don't marry a position.

Contrarian Investing: Be Fearful When Ot.description: Be fearful when others are greedy; crowd extremes and manias often mark turning points.

Analyze Financial Statements Before Inve.description: Read the income statement, balance sheet and cash flows before buying a company.

Supply and Demand Drive Price.description: Every price move reflects an imbalance between buyers and sellers.

Buy Low, Sell High (Value Investing).description: Buy assets below their intrinsic value; a cheap price alone is not value.

Accept Losses as a Cost of Doing Busines.display_name: Accept Losses as a Cost of Business
Accept Losses as a Cost of Doing Busines.description: Losses are inevitable and expected; treating them as failures leads to worse decisions.

Adapt Strategy to Market Conditions.description: Trending, ranging and volatile markets reward different approaches; filter for regime first.

Diversify Across Asset Classes.description: Spread capital across stocks, bonds, cash and others, and rebalance to target weights.

Avoid Overtrading.description: Too many trades or markets raise costs and lower quality; take breaks.

Earnings Growth Drives Stock Price.description: Over time, share prices follow the growth of company earnings.

Assess Management Quality and Competitiv.description: Durable advantages and capable, honest management protect long-term returns.

Don't Average Down on a Losing Position.description: Adding to a losing position compounds the mistake instead of fixing it.

Invest in Companies You Understand.description: Stay within your circle of competence so you can judge the business.

Compound Interest / Reinvest Returns.description: Reinvested gains grow exponentially; time in the market is the key input.

Time Decay (Theta) Erodes Option Value.description: Options lose value each day, faster near expiry, which favors sellers over time.

Avoid Revenge Trading After a Loss.description: Trying to win back a loss right away leads to oversized, unplanned trades.

Set Clear Financial Goals.description: Know why you invest or trade and what you are aiming for.

Live Below Your Means / Save Consistentl.display_name: Live Below Your Means / Save Consistently
Live Below Your Means / Save Consistentl.description: Steady saving builds the capital that investing then compounds.

Dollar-Cost Averaging.description: Invest a fixed amount at regular intervals to smooth out entry prices.

Margin of Safety When Valuing a Stock.description: Buy well below estimated value so errors in your estimate don't cause losses.

Avoid High-Interest Consumer Debt.description: Paying off expensive debt is a guaranteed return few investments beat.

Elliott Wave Analysis.description: Markets move in five-wave impulses and three-wave corrections, which some use to forecast turns.

Build an Emergency Fund.description: Cash reserves prevent forced selling at bad times.

Avoid Curve-Fitting / Over-Optimizing a.description: Over-optimized backtests fit past noise and fail live; distrust unverified results.

Pay Yourself First.description: Save before spending, not from what is left over.

Seasonal and Calendar Patterns.description: Effects like "Sell in May," the January effect and the presidential cycle show recurring tendencies.

Use Trailing Stops to Lock In Profits.description: Move the stop with price to lock in gains while giving the trade room.

Be Skeptical of Gurus, Tips and Hype.display_name: Be Skeptical of Gurus, Tips and Hype
Be Skeptical of Gurus, Tips and Hype.description: Think independently; tips, newsletters and brokers often have conflicts.

Match Your Trading Method to Your Person.display_name: Match Your Method to Your Personality
Match Your Trading Method to Your Person.description: A system you can't follow comfortably will be abandoned at the worst moment.

Market Breadth and Sentiment Indicators.description: Advance-decline lines, put/call ratios and the VIX confirm trends or flag extremes.

Pyramid Into Winning Positions.description: Add to winners in smaller increments, never to losers.

Quantify Portfolio Risk (VaR, Std Dev, S.description: Use standard deviation, value-at-risk and stress tests to measure exposure.

Understand Order Types; Prefer Limit Ord.display_name: Understand Order Types; Prefer Limit Orders
Understand Order Types; Prefer Limit Ord.description: Order choice and routing affect fill prices and costs.

Arbitrage and Market-Neutral Strategies.description: Pairs, merger and convertible arbitrage profit from price gaps between related assets.

Bollinger Bands for Volatility Extremes.description: Volatility bands flag stretched prices and volatility squeezes.

Follow Insider and Institutional Activit.description: Insider buying, buybacks and commercial positioning (COT) hint at informed views.

Kelly Criterion / Optimal f Position Siz.description: Formulas that size bets by edge and odds to maximize long-run growth.

Price Action Over Indicators; Use Multip.display_name: Price Action Over Indicators; Seek Confirmation
Price Action Over Indicators; Use Multip.description: Require several tools to agree rather than trusting one signal.

Scale In and Out of Positions.display_name: Scale In and Out of Positions
Scale In and Out of Positions.description: Enter and take profits in parts to reduce timing risk.

Sector Rotation With the Economic Cycle.display_name: Sector Rotation With the Economic Cycle
Sector Rotation With the Economic Cycle.description: Different sectors lead at different cycle stages; analyze top-down.

Divergence Between Price and Indicators.description: When price makes a new high but momentum doesn't, the trend may be tiring.

Minimize Fees, Costs and Taxes.description: Costs compound against you as surely as returns compound for you.

Avoid Trading Around High-Volatility New.description: Releases cause erratic spikes; "buy the rumor, sell the news."

Concentrate in High-Conviction Ideas.description: Some argue few well-researched positions beat over-diversification.

Guard Against Cognitive Biases.description: Overconfidence, anchoring, hindsight and loss aversion distort decisions.

Know and Define Your Trading Edge.display_name: Know and Define Your Trading Edge
Know and Define Your Trading Edge.description: Be able to state why your setup should make money.

Avoid Choppy / Range-Bound Markets.description: Trend systems bleed in sideways markets.

Reflexivity: Markets Can Stay Irrational.description: Perceptions feed back into fundamentals, and mispricing can outlast your capital.

Relative Strength: Buy Market Leaders.description: Stocks outperforming the market tend to keep doing so.

Tactical Asset Allocation on Valuation.description: Shift allocations based on valuation or index timing signals.

Time Trades to the Best Market Sessions.display_name: Time Trades to the Best Sessions
Time Trades to the Best Market Sessions.description: Liquidity and movement concentrate in certain hours.

Treat Each Trade as Statistically Indepe.description: Past outcomes don't change the next trade's odds; avoid martingale doubling.

Evaluate Fund Managers and Performance P.description: Use time-weighted total returns and due diligence when choosing managers.

Maintain Physical and Mental Health.description: Sleep, exercise and stress control support decision quality.

Mean Reversion and Fading Moves.description: Bet on stretched prices returning toward the average.

Practice With Paper Trading First.description: Use a demo account before risking real money.

Price Gaps and Gap Trading.description: Gaps often fill, or signal continuation or exhaustion.

Short Selling.description: Profit from falling prices by selling borrowed shares.

Swing Trading.description: Hold positions for days to capture short-term swings.

Valuation Models (DCF, Real Options).description: Value a business on discounted future cash flows and the worth of its flexibility.

Acting In Your Own Best Interest.display_name: Acting in Your Own Best Interest

Automated Trading Systems.description: letting code execute rules to remove discretion.

Avoid Trading in Contract Delivery Month.display_name: Avoid Trading in Contract Delivery Months
Avoid Trading in Contract Delivery Month.description: futures liquidity and delivery risk rise near expiry.

Basic Options Strategies (Calls, Puts, S.description: long calls and puts, covered writes, and bull and bear spreads.

Ladder Bond Maturities to Manage Reinves.description: stagger maturities to manage reinvestment risk.

Market Profile and Value-Area Analysis.description: reading where volume clusters by price.

Small-Cap Return Premiums May Be Illusor.description: the size premium can vanish after costs and liquidity.

Special Situations: Reverse Mergers and.display_name: Special Situations: Reverse Mergers and Shell Companies
